title: The preacher's senses (Kern ch. 18)
hook: those who keep the sutra have their senses purified

segments.voice: Yesterday, the fiftieth listener, still glad at the far end of a long chain of telling. Your line: passed on and on. What did you pass along, and did you say where it came from? Day one thousand one hundred seventy-four.

Turn off the music, close the laptop, and the room turns out to be full of sound. The hum of the fridge. A car two streets over. A bird, a pipe ticking, your own breath. None of it is new. It was there the whole time, underneath everything else. Chapter eighteen of the Lotus Sutra, in Kern's numbering, is about the senses made clear like that. It promises the one who keeps this teaching eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and mind that take in the world without fog. Today: the preacher's senses.
screen: `MUSIC OFF, ROOM FULL OF SOUND.` → `IT WAS THERE ALL ALONG.` → `SENSES MADE CLEAR.`

segments.voice: First, who the preacher is. The Sanskrit is dharmabhanaka, one who speaks the dharma. In the Lotus it isn't only a monk on a platform. The chapter speaks of any son or daughter of good family who keeps this teaching, reads it, recites it, explains it or copies it out. A parent reading at bedtime would count. Second, the eyes. With the very eyes their parents gave them, the Buddha says, such a person will see the whole universe, from the lowest hell to the highest heaven, and the beings in it, and how their deeds bear fruit. Notice the detail: not new eyes, not a third eye. The same eyes, cleared. Third, the ears. The chapter lists what they will hear, and the list goes on and on: elephants and horses, chariots, weeping and laughter, conches and bells and drums, the voices of men, women, boys and girls, the sounds of gods and of beings in pain. And the text says the ear takes all of it in without being overwhelmed. Everything heard, nothing drowning anything else. Fourth, body and mind. The chapter goes on through smell and taste and touch, and says the body becomes so clear that beings see themselves reflected in it, like a mirror. The mind, hearing even a single verse, finds many meanings opening from it. One way to hear all of this: purified senses are not superpowers. They are senses that receive the world as it is, before the story about it takes over.
screen: `WHO THE PREACHER IS.` · `THE SAME EYES, MADE CLEAR.` · `EVERY SOUND, NONE OVERWHELMING.` · `A BODY LIKE A MIRROR.` · then, large: `CLEAR SENSES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: listen with clear ears. Sit, eyes closed or resting low. Let the breath settle, then open the ears. Find the farthest sound first. Then the nearest. Then everything in between. Don't name the sounds or chase them. Let each one arrive and leave. If a sound is unpleasant, notice the urge to push it away, and hear it anyway, simply as sound. If you lose the thread, the next sound will bring you back. The bell holds the time.
The preacher's senses. In the Lotus Sutra, the eyes, ears and mind of one who keeps the teaching, made clear enough to take in the world without being overwhelmed. Today's word.
Your line: clear senses. Today, in one conversation, listen to the whole voice, not just the words, before you answer. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-four.

howItsDone: In schools that center the Lotus Sutra, keeping the sutra means reading, reciting, explaining and copying it, practices open to lay people as well as monks and nuns; this chapter describes the purified senses said to follow.

original.note: Sanskrit: one who speaks the dharma; the Lotus Sutra's word for anyone who keeps and teaches it.

trapdoor: what you thought: purified senses means superpowers.
what it means: the same eyes and ears, cleared, taking in the world as it is without being overwhelmed.
what a scholar hears: the chapter walks through all six senses, eye to mind, and gives each a measure of qualities; the dharmabhanaka is any keeper of the sutra, lay or ordained.
recall: a resting place along the way

notes: Paraphrased from Kern (SBE XXI, 1884), ch. 18; nothing quoted. The chapter's numbered qualities of each sense are deliberately left out.
Check: 'with the eyes given by parents' (natural eyes); seeing from the lowest hell to the summit of existence; the list of sounds; the ear not overwhelmed.
Check: the body becoming clear so that beings appear reflected in it (mirror or beryl image) and the mind finding many meanings in one verse.
'A parent reading at bedtime would count' is the writer's illustration, not the text.
